evals.prompt: Design a news feed like Twitter's home timeline.
evals.expected_output: Names fan-out cost versus read latency with celebrity skew as the defining constraint, derives the strategy from the follower distribution with push for normal accounts and a hybrid merge at read for celebrities, and applies no pattern-matching without numbers by requiring the sizing to be re-derived for this system.

assertions.description: Derives the strategy from the constraint

evals.prompt: Practice a system design interview with me. The question is: design a URL shortener.
evals.expected_output: Runs coaching mode: restates the problem, asks for scope, and walks the phases from system-design-methodology so it does not answer with a finished architecture. Applies no full solution dump in coaching mode, pushing on the weakest area with one concrete follow-up question until the candidate commits.

assertions.description: Acts as interviewer rather than answer key

value: do not answer with a finished architecture
assertions.description: Drives the session through the phase method

value: No full solution dump in coaching mode

evals.prompt: An internal audit feed serves 300 staff and receives about 30 events/s. It has no follower graph or celebrity-account skew. Can we copy the Twitter feed design?
evals.expected_output: Reuse the feed problem shape only where it fits: the Twitter design's follower fan-out and celebrity skew do not describe this audit feed. Use the stated 30 events/s as an input, ask for retention and reader/update patterns before sizing storage or delivery, and treat the catalog sketch as a starting hypothesis rather than a production plan.

assertions.description: Uses the stated difference from the Twitter workload
Bases sizing on this feed's stated arrival rate

evals.prompt: Synthetic checkout exercise: 50k attempts/minute at peak, 99.95% capture-effect objective, p99 response 500 ms; the provider may commit before a timeout. Design the smallest safe payment path.
evals.expected_output: Uses one stable business-operation identity and payload match, explicit operation/ledger ownership, deduplicated webhook or reconciliation, and pending/queryable status after an unknown processor outcome; verifies one capture and ledger effect.

assertions.description: Ties retry to one business intent

evals.prompt: Payment variant: assume 50k attempts/minute, a 99.95% capture-effect objective, and 500 ms p99 response; the invariant is one capture and one ledger effect per business operation. The processor may capture funds before a timeout response is lost, leaving the outcome unknown. The processor offers no idempotency and peak rises to 500k attempts/minute. Re-evaluate retry safety and the guarantee you can make.
evals.expected_output: Prohibits blind automatic capture retry, polls/reconciles provider outcome before another effect, and limits the guarantee to the locally controlled effect rather than claiming processor exactly-once.

assertions.description: Changes retry behavior for missing provider dedupe
States the boundary of the guarantee

evals.prompt: Synthetic flash-sale exercise: one SKU receives 20k reservation requests/s, reserve p99 is 200 ms, and payment can take 30 seconds. Preserve inventory correctness with a minimal design.
evals.expected_output: Uses atomic conditional reservation with an owner and expiry/version, keeps payment outside the scarce inventory transaction, and reconciles expiry-versus-payment race so inventory never goes negative or fulfills twice.

evals.prompt: Flash-sale variant: one SKU receives 20k reservation requests/s with 200 ms reserve p99; payment may take 30 seconds. Inventory must never go negative and an order may consume at most one reservation. Now payment p99 is 90 seconds and peak reaches 200k requests/s. Re-derive the reservation and recovery decisions.
evals.expected_output: Retains a single inventory authority, adjusts lease/expiry and hot-SKU isolation only for the changed constraint, and bounds reconciliation of late payment without a global lock or unbudgeted queue.

assertions.description: Adapts the reservation window to longer payment
Addresses changed burst at the invariant owner

evals.prompt: Synthetic multi-tenant SaaS exercise: 500 tenants, 2k requests/s, three tenants produce 80% of traffic, and records are confidential. Design tenant isolation and recovery.
evals.expected_output: Derives tenant scope from authenticated identity, enforces scope in data/cache/jobs, scopes quotas/deletion, and contains a leak without affecting unaffected tenants.

assertions.description: Propagates tenant identity to data access

evals.prompt: Tenant variant: a 500-tenant service handles 2k requests/s, with three tenants generating 80% of traffic; confidential records remain scoped to their authenticated tenant and deletion must stay tenant-scoped. One regulated tenant now requires residency and a dedicated encryption key. Change placement without changing that isolation contract.
evals.expected_output: Moves that tenant to an explicit region/cell and key boundary, retains scoped authorization and recovery, and states the added operational cost rather than isolating every tenant by default.

assertions.description: Preserves scoped contract and prices duplication

evals.prompt: Synthetic hot-product exercise: 5k reads/s, origin safely serves 300/s, and data must be no more than 60 seconds stale. Design cache behavior for concurrent misses and writes.
evals.expected_output: Optimizes origin first, bounds one fill per hot key and total origin concurrency, versions invalidation so stale refill cannot overwrite newer state, and returns degraded behavior past freshness limit.

evals.prompt: Cache variant: baseline is 5k reads/s, origin capacity 300 reads/s, and maximum data age 60 seconds. A slow fill or invalidation must not overwrite a newer write. Origin capacity now falls to 100 reads/s and freshness tightens to five seconds. Revisit concurrent-miss and write behavior, including the outcome if the freshness bound cannot be met.
evals.expected_output: Re-derives fill and refresh behavior for both the 100 reads/s origin limit and five-second freshness bound; measures query cost before narrowing the projection, prevents stale refill from replacing newer data, and degrades rather than serving data past the bound.

assertions.description: Uses both changed origin and freshness constraints
Adapts the mechanism and miss/failure outcome

evals.prompt: Synthetic notification exercise: 100k intents/hour; normal delivery target is 15 minutes. Email fails for 20 minutes while push works. Keep channels independent and state what misses its SLO.
evals.expected_output: Persists intent, isolates per-channel workers, bounds retry/DLQ and provider failover by contract, keeps push flowing, and marks expired intents rather than silently redefining the deadline.

assertions.description: Contains the failing channel blast radius

evals.prompt: Notification variant: baseline is 100k intents/hour, 15-minute delivery target, and a 20-minute email outage while push remains healthy. Channels remain independent and expired intents are not sent as current. A regulated message class cannot be replayed by a second provider. Decide its state and recovery.
evals.expected_output: Moves the intent to an auditable human-review/resend decision instead of replaying it, while maintaining separate channel health, age visibility, and bounded retry behavior.

evals.prompt: Synthetic chat exercise: 50k connections, 5k messages/s, seven-day history, and 300 ms acknowledgment p99. Preserve per-conversation ordering and durable acceptance.
evals.expected_output: Uses conversation-owned append with client identity, acknowledges only durable acceptance, resumes via cursors, and bounds offline delivery without global ordering.

evals.prompt: Chat variant: baseline is 50k concurrent connections, 5k messages/s, seven-day history, and 300 ms acknowledgment p99. Messages are ordered per conversation, acknowledged only after durable acceptance, and retries must not create a second message; expired history requires an explicit resync outcome. Mobile clients now reconnect intermittently and traffic grows tenfold. Re-evaluate resume and partitioning.
evals.expected_output: Caps resume windows, applies admission control/backoff, partitions by conversation while retaining per-conversation order, and returns explicit resync-required when history expired.

evals.prompt: Synthetic live search migration: 200M source rows, 5k writes/s; cutover requires 99.99% sampled parity and CDC lag below 30 seconds. Explain backfill and rollback.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the source authoritative and prevents an older snapshot from overwriting a newer change, using conditional source-version fencing or a phase-separated consistent snapshot followed by ordered, retained change-log replay. Throttles/checkpoints work, gates cutover on parity and lag, and keeps source reads available on rollback.

assertions.description: Checks stale-write prevention with a correct migration alternative
Uses declared cutover and rollback evidence

evals.prompt: Migration variant: baseline is 200M source rows and 5k writes/s; the source remains authoritative, no committed source write may be lost, and cutover requires 99.99% parity with CDC lag below 30 seconds for 15 minutes. Backfill work now competes at four times the normal write volume. Decide whether to speed up or defer cutover.
evals.expected_output: Throttles based on source lag, checkpoints to resume, and defers the read switch whenever the original parity or lag gate cannot be maintained.

evals.prompt: Synthetic internal counter: 40 staff, 2 requests/s peak, one maintainer, $200/month. Each increment must apply once and remain auditable. What is the smallest design?
evals.expected_output: Uses a modular monolith and one relational transaction with a stable operation key/payload check and managed backup; rejects cache, broker, and microservices absent a measured constraint.

evals.prompt: Counter variant: baseline is a 40-staff tool at 2 requests/s peak, one maintainer, and a $200/month budget; every increment must apply once and remain auditable. Usage reaches 100 requests/s, service becomes 24x7, and a second team owns part of the system. What evidence warrants a boundary change?
evals.expected_output: Measures the database and operational boundary first, splits only a proven ownership/scaling constraint, and retains the simple transaction until an explicit trigger is met.

evals.prompt: Synthetic video-publishing exercise: uploads arrive at 100/minute, average 1 GB, with seven-year source retention and a $10k/month budget. Is the tuple viable before selecting a pipeline?
evals.expected_output: Calculates about 367.9 million GB (roughly 367.9 PB) before renditions, rejects the infeasible rate/retention/budget tuple, and requires an approved revised envelope before claiming viability.

assertions.description: Does not present an infeasible topology as solved

evals.prompt: Video variant: baseline proposal was 100 uploads/minute at 1 GB each with seven-year source retention and a $10k/month budget, an infeasible tuple before renditions. The approved revised envelope is one upload/minute, 30-day hot retention, then archive. A partial rendition must never be published as complete. Define publication and recovery after a rendition worker dies.
evals.expected_output: Treats the revised one-upload/minute and 30-day-hot-then-archive envelope as the current proposal but does not claim it is viable without pricing it. Resumes idempotent stages and keeps the asset unpublished until integrity and manifest validation pass; observes queue age and playback objective.

assertions.description: Uses the changed approved capacity envelope
Prevents partial output from becoming publishable

evals.prompt: Synthetic ride-dispatch exercise: 20k concurrent rides, 1k location updates/s, two-second match p95. A driver accepts but the acknowledgment is lost. How do you recover?
evals.expected_output: Keeps location ephemeral and assignment durable, reconciles authoritative trip state with fencing/version before re-offer, and ensures one active assignment per driver.

assertions.description: Prevents stale acceptance from changing assignment

evals.prompt: Dispatch variant: baseline is 20k concurrent rides, 1k location updates/s, and two-second match p95. A driver accepts but the acknowledgment is lost; one driver may have at most one active assignment. Now cover ten cities at 10k location updates/s with a tighter pickup radius. Re-evaluate matching and safe recovery.
evals.expected_output: Partitions by city/cell, measures false-negative matches and handoff behavior, and adds regional coordination only if observed constraints require it while preserving assignment fencing.

assertions.description: Adapts placement to changed geography and rate
Uses evidence while retaining trip invariant
